provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 closes the petition with a full stop before Qui vivis; 1962 sets a colon (illustra:); 1862's conclusion cue stops at 'cum Deo Patre.'; 1962 prints 'cum Deo Patre in unitate.'; OCR noise only: 'AUrem' for the ornamental A at 13704, 'nostne' and 'tiue' for nostrae and tuae. Corroboration: Venice 1570 (degraded-latin; the edition's own record forbids resting a claim or a negative on a raw search over it, so this is corroboration only and nothing here rests on it) at text-layer lines 6459-6467, where the layer drops 'et' and mangles 'gratia' ('accommoda: mentis nostre te-/nebras ere tue visitationis/illustra. Qui viuis et regnas cum.'). I read it but I do not rely on it: on its own bytes it would not establish this clause..

propers.text:
Aurem tuam, quaesumus, Domine, precibus nostris accommoda: et mentis nostrae
tenebras gratia tuae visitationis illustra: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo
Patre in unitate.
